depicted_variant: Human-shaped enshrined Japanese court spirit, inspired by Prince Sawara calamity account
prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Square mature painterly mythology encyclopedia artwork. GORYŌ, a tragically dead Japanese aristocratic spirit associated with calamity and appeasing shrines, inspired by Prince Sawara's account. One mature human-shaped male court spirit in historically plausible late Nara/early Heian formal dark layered court robes and tall plain black court cap, dignified resentful expression and normal human face/hands. Standing almost still before a small ancient Kyoto shrine beyond an empty dirt courtyard, nighttime storm clouds and ominous rolling mist. Slight translucent robe edges show he is an apparition; all bodily proportions remain coherent and human. No invented deformities, monstrous eyes, fangs, claws, ghost tentacles or weapon; no epidemic victims or modern architecture. Elegant detailed brushwork with atmospheric depth, restrained antique-gold light and forest-green shadows. Main heads and hands entirely contained in frame. No text, border, signature, watermark, gore, nudity or unintended extra limbs.
visual_requirements: Heian court clothing and Kyoto shrine context
Calamity atmosphere without invented monstrous anatomy
aura: Solemn unsettling shrine apparition under storm clouds
nonhuman_features: Tragically dead spirit placated through enshrinement, linked to calamity; no anatomical deformation claimed
historical_basis: Goryō are spirits of tragically dead people linked to calamity and later enshrined as kami. Prince Sawara is one documented instance; human appearance in period court dress is an illustrative choice rather than a source-prescribed anatomy.
artistic_changes: Exact human facial appearance, costume, landscape or architecture, spectral rendering, scale placement and illumination are artistic choices; no additional anatomical claim introduced.

visual_review.notes: Individually viewed original: one human-shaped male court spirit with tall black cap and layered formal robes, pale solemn normal face and two coherent hands, misty lower robe, small shrine behind under storm clouds. No distorted anatomy, claws, horns or writing. Costume ornament and shrine architecture are interpretive, not a portrait claim of Prince Sawara.
